summary: Practise catchment analysis, HEC-HMS scenarios, and model evaluation in five days. Explore hydrology and hydrological modeling training.
lede: Hydrology training covers how rainfall, catchment conditions, and streamflow evidence inform runoff estimates and model decisions. For hydrologists, water resources engineers, and flood-risk analysts, practical work includes mapping catchments in QGIS, preparing and checking inputs, configuring rainfall-runoff scenarios in HEC-HMS, and assessing model fit, sensitivity, and uncertainty to explain results.
audienceIntro: This intermediate course is designed for professionals who prepare, review, or rely on rainfall-runoff estimates. It is particularly relevant when you must explain catchment assumptions, model fit, and uncertainty to colleagues who use hydrological modeling results. This course is designed for: Catchment Hydrologists who turn rainfall records into defensible streamflow estimates. Water Resources Engineers who assess runoff inputs for planning studies. Flood Risk Analysts who compare event scenarios and peak-flow estimates. Hydrological Modelers who configure and document rainfall-runoff simulations. Hydrometric Specialists who screen gauge records before model calibration. Stormwater Engineers who assess catchment response to design rainfall. Watershed Managers who review land-cover assumptions in runoff forecasts. Water Resources Planning Leads who present model uncertainty to decision-makers. GIS Analysts for Water Resources who prepare catchment boundaries and spatial inputs. Environmental Impact Assessment Specialists who review modeled changes in streamflow.
modules: Hydrological Modeling and WMO Catchment Context
NRCS Curve Number and FAO-56 Inputs
Hydrological Modeling Results and HEC-HMS Reporting
prerequisites: You should have working knowledge of rainfall-runoff processes, basic hydrograph interpretation, and spreadsheet calculations. Hydrological modeling exercises use HEC-HMS and QGIS; coding is not required. Access to a laptop suitable for the digital exercises and any software-installation arrangements should be confirmed before the course.
